arm-A.title: Trinity's escape across the rooftops to the phone
arm-A.summary: Morpheus tells Trinity the traced hardline is cut and she must reach the Wells and Lake phone instead. She bolts through a hall where Agent Brown appears and out a broken window onto the fire escape, only to find Agent Smith waiting in the alley below, forcing her up onto the roof. She runs the rooftops with cold grace while the cops flounder and Brown duplicates her leap across the 40-foot gap, then she dives through a lit window, crashes down a stairwell, and races the garbage truck to the booth. She answers the Wells and Lake phone and is gone before the truck destroys the booth. On the street, the Agents convert the loss into a colder victory: the informant is real and they now have the next target's name.

state_triples.reading: Trinity's escape is a study in managed fear: she registers each blow — the cut line, the Agents, the blocked alley — and then deliberately re-collects herself into a soldier executing orders. Her calm on the roof is not the absence of fear but a decision not to let it touch her movement, the same self-regulation she showed taking a deep breath in the hotel. What the whole run reveals is that she is betting everything on the physics of this world being real — that a 40-foot gap is a wall to her pursuers — and the horror beneath her discipline is that she.

state_triples.reading: Smith's is the event's true pivot. His frustration at losing Trinity again is real and bodily — jaw set, grinding his molars — but it flips the instant Brown confirms the informant is real: he almost smiles, and the failure stops mattering because a colder pleasure has arrived. arm-B.title: Trinity's escape across the rooftops to the phone
arm-B.summary: Morpheus confirms Trinity's hotel hardline is cut and directs her to a phone at Wells and Lake. She runs the building's exterior to the street — hall, fire escape, roof, across the rooftops, and down through a window into a back stairwell — while the Agents pursue and match her. She reaches a ringing booth on the street and is gone before a garbage truck crushes it, so the Agents are left with wreckage and no body, but with the crew's next target named as Neo.
arm-B.action: After Morpheus confirms the hotel hardline is cut and directs her to a phone at Wells and Lake, Trinity bursts into the hall into Agent Brown and his police unit and flees she plummets through the shattered glass and onto the fire escape. Finding Agent Smith waiting in the alley below, she climbs to the roof and runs the rooftops, clearing a 40-foot gap the cops cannot follow while Agent Brown duplicates the leap with the same unnatural grace. She launches from the roof's edge toward a lit window, dives, crashes through glass into a back stairwell, and — finding only wind where she expects Brown — gets to her feet despite her injuries. On the street she races a U-turning garbage truck to a ringing phone booth, answers it, and is gone before the truck pulverizes the booth; the Agents inspect the wreckage with no body, but leave with the next target named as Neo.

arm-A.title: Trinity's escape across the rooftops to the phone
arm-A.summary: Morpheus tells Trinity the traced hardline is cut and she must reach the Wells and Lake phone instead. She bolts through a hall where Agent Brown appears and out a broken window onto the fire escape, only to find Agent Smith waiting in the alley below, forcing her up onto the roof. She runs the rooftops with cold grace while the cops flounder and Brown duplicates her leap across the 40-foot gap, then she dives through a lit window, crashes down a stairwell, and races the garbage truck to the booth. She answers the Wells and Lake phone and is gone before the truck destroys the booth. On the street, the Agents convert the loss into a colder victory: the informant is real and they now have the next target's name.
arm-A.action: Trinity loses her hardline exit and is driven across the rooftops to the Wells and Lake phone, escaping the Agents only because the machine's hunt has already shifted to a new target.

state_triples.reading: Trinity's escape is a study in managed fear: she registers each blow — the cut line, the Agents, the blocked alley — and then deliberately re-collects herself into a soldier executing orders. What the whole run reveals is that she is betting everything on the physics of this world being real — that a 40-foot gap is a wall to her pursuers — and the horror beneath her discipline is that she.

arm-A.title: Neo is summoned and drawn toward the truth
arm-A.summary: Alone in his apartment one night, Neo is contacted through his own PC by an unseen party that types messages the machine should not produce, ending with 'Follow the white rabbit' — and, on cue, a real knock answers the screen. He runs a disk-for-cash deal with Choi and Dujour as usual, but after the visitors leave he can no longer trust whether he is awake or dreaming. Dujour's small white rabbit pin then pulls him out against his better judgment, and at a crowded apartment gathering Trinity — a woman who names herself as the Trinity who breached the I.R.S. database — tells him she was on his computer, warns that he is being watched and in danger, and refuses to give him the answer because it has to be seen to be believed; when Neo asks 'What is the Matrix?' she says the answer is out there and will find him, then withdraws and leaves him standing amid the crowd as a sound closes over him.
arm-A.action: The screen at Neo's PC blanks and types its own messages — 'Wake up, Neo,' 'The Matrix has you,' 'Follow the white rabbit,' 'Knock, knock, Neo' — and a real knock meets the last one. Still unnerved, Neo keeps the chain on, retrieves a disk from a hollowed Baudrillard, takes Choi's 'two grand,' and completes the sale. After Choi jokes the night is mescaline and that he needs to 'unplug,' Neo is hit by a returning 'feeling of unrealness' and asks whether Choi has ever been unsure he was awake. arm-B.title: Neo is summoned and drawn toward the truth
arm-B.summary: Alone in his technology-crammed apartment, Neo is jolted from sleep by his own PC typing messages at him that end with a real knock answering the screen, leaving him unable to tell whether he was awake or dreaming. He still closes a disk-for-cash deal with Choi through his chained, multi-locked door, but the visit leaves him hollowed by a returning sense of unrealness, and when Dujour proposes taking him out he refuses until he spots a small white rabbit pin on her jacket, at which the room seems to tilt and he agrees. At a smoke-filled gathering of people dressed in black, Trinity walks straight up to him, names herself as the hacker who was on his computer, warns him that he is in danger and being watched, and reframes his sleepless solitude as a search for a hidden figure and an answer no one can be told. Pressing close in the deafening music, she withholds the substance and instead gives him the question, which he finally voices aloud before she melts back into the crowd, leaving him with the promise that the answer is out there and will find him.
arm-B.action: Neo is woken at his PC by messages that type themselves on his screen and end with a knock that answers the last line, cracking his cause-and-effect certainty and blurring the machine into the real. He performs normalcy, opening his series of locks and chain to complete a disk-for-cash deal with Choi, then is left hollowed by a recurring wave of unrealness. He refuses Dujour's offer to go out until the white rabbit pin on her jacket flips him into motion, and he arrives at the party out of place, beer in hand. Trinity approaches, names herself as the one who was on his computer, warns him he is being watched and in danger, and turns his private, sleepless obsession into a directed search, pressing close in the loud music until he voices What is the Matrix? and is told the answer can only be seen, not explained. She then withdraws into the shifting crowd, leaving him alone with the question and the promise that the answer will find him.
